name: SSIM Map Analysis
description: Computes local SSIM structural similarity maps to detect region-level quality inconsistencies (Wang et al., 2004).
mechanism:
This method applies the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) framework by Wang et al. (2004) for forensic quality analysis:

1. **Local Statistics Computation**: For each local window w (typically 11×11 Gaussian), three components are computed: luminance μ, contrast σ, and structure σ_xy. These capture perceptually relevant image properties following the human visual system model.

2. **SSIM Component Decomposition**: The SSIM index between reference and test patches decomposes as: SSIM(x,y) = l(x,y)^α · c(x,y)^β · s(x,y)^γ, where l = (2μₓμᵧ+C₁)/(μₓ²+μᵧ²+C₁), c = (2σₓσᵧ+C₂)/(σₓ²+σᵧ²+C₂), s = (σₓᵧ+C₃)/(σₓσᵧ+C₃).

3. **Self-Similarity Map Construction**: For forensic analysis without a reference image, local self-similarity is computed by comparing each patch against its neighboring regions. The resulting SSIM map reveals spatial consistency of image quality — genuine images show smooth, physically coherent quality variation.

4. **Quality Discontinuity Detection**: Abrupt changes in local SSIM indicate potential manipulation boundaries — where inserted or AI-generated regions meet authentic image content. These discontinuities arise from differences in compression artifacts, noise levels, or rendering quality.

5. **Statistical Profiling**: The distribution of local SSIM values is analyzed. Natural images exhibit characteristic SSIM distributions governed by content complexity. AI-generated images often show abnormally uniform local quality (lacking the natural variation from optics, sensor, and compression) or suspicious quality boundaries absent in untampered photographs.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
